emily (eng-security): Heads-up: triage found two relevant CVEs impacting our container rootfs. CVE-2026-1122 (glibc heap overflow) hits Ubuntu 22.04 base images; CVE-2025-9876 (OpenSSL timing leak) affects Alpine 3.18 builds. Both rated HIGH by upstream.

michael (eng-sre): Thanks. Any PoC or exploitability notes?

emily (eng-security): Upstream notes: glibc CVE needs patched glibc >= 2.35. Exploit requires local code execution in container process but can be triggered via crafted network input in some server daemons. OpenSSL one is a side-channel leaking session keys in TLS handshakes under certain ciphers suites.

jordan (eng-runtime): Summary for us: Ubuntu images need glibc rebuild; Alpine needs OpenSSL rebuild + musl check. We should avoid mass rolling both at once. Recommend a staged plan: rebuild images -> sign -> push to staging registry -> canary to 5% traffic -> monitor.

anna (platform): Agreed. Also: signing hooks and KMS rotation. We need to ensure the signing key hasn't changed or if changed we update trust bundles in clusters. Who will handle key rotation? @michael?

michael (eng-sre): I can handle KMS signing rotation. Proposal: reuse existing key, but create a new signing key pair (key-v2) in KMS and sign new images with v2. Update ImagePolicy admission controllers to accept both v1 and v2 for 48 hours, then retire v1.

emily (eng-security): Good. Prioritization: glibc CVE higher blast radius for stateful backend services and sidecars. Mark services that run as root or expose network ports as P0. List I/O: auth, api-gateway, embeddings-worker.

jordan (eng-runtime): I'll produce patched base images. Plan: two pipelines — ubuntu-22.04-glibc-patch and alpine-3.18-openssl-patch. Each pipeline will: checkout base Dockerfile, apt update + build glibc from distro package, run regression tests, generate SBOM, sign image.

jordan (eng-runtime): Dockerfile snippet we'll use:

```
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libc6
# ensure package version >= patched
```

jordan (eng-runtime): For alpine:

```
FROM alpine:3.18
RUN apk add --no-cache openssl
# validate openssl version >= patched
```

michael (eng-sre): Canary policy: rollout to canary k8s pool (label: canary=security-patch). Traffic shaping: 5% for 1h, 25% for 3h, 100% if no regressions. Auto-rollback on error budget or P99 latency regression >15%.

emily (eng-security): Add security checks to pipeline: run snyk/oval scans, run internalsql fuzzer against auth and api-gateway containers, verify CVE absent in SBOM. Also increment audit logging for canary traffic.

anna (platform): About audit logs and RBAC: we need to ensure image promotion events and signing actions write to audit logs and only CI-bot/service-account has sign permission. I'll add a new IAM role `image-signer` restricted to KMS:Encrypt/Sign for the key. RBAC in clusters: `admission-controller` service account needs read-only access to trust bundle.

michael (eng-sre): I'll create KMS key key-rootfs-v2, restrict to CI project, and add a rotation schedule (30d). I'll post key ARN once created.

deploy-bot: pipeline triggered: ubuntu-22.04-glibc-patch build #123 queued by jordan

jordan (eng-runtime): Tests planned: unit, integration (grpc/tls), performance smoke (P50/P95), SBOM diff to confirm no extra packages. Also will run canary pods with strace and heap checks for glibc.

emily (eng-security): For OpenSSL timing leak, add TLS handshake trace regression. If our ingress offloads TLS (cloud provider), we must verify provider patched too. Flag existing external TLS endpoints as potentially vulnerable and open ticket to provider.

michael (eng-sre): Good catch. I'll file ticket to cloud-net with list of LB endpoints.

anna (platform): Promotion flow: staging tag -> signed:staging -> registry promotion -> signed:canary -> clusters pick up via ImagePolicy. We will keep previous images available for rollback. Also will add an automated manifest label: `security.cve/1759223345=true` for tracking.

jordan (eng-runtime): CLI commands we'll use for canary control:

```
# promote image to canary
curl -X POST https://registry.internal/promote -d '{"image":"repo/base:patched","target":"canary"}'
# pause rollout
kubectl rollout pause deploy/api-gateway -n prod
# roll forward
kubectl set image deploy/api-gateway api=repo/base:patched -n prod
```

michael (eng-sre): Monitoring: wire up alerts for pod crashes, core dumps, TLS handshake errors, and spike in CPU/latency for canary namespace. Send alerts to #incidents and tag @oncall.

emily (eng-security): Timeline proposal: start builds now, canary for Ubuntu tomorrow 09:00 UTC, Alpine the day after if no regressions. If critical, we can accelerate Alpine earlier.

jordan (eng-runtime): I'll kick off ubuntu pipeline now. Expect image + SBOM in ~45m.

deploy-bot: ubuntu-22.04-glibc-patch build #123 started by jordan at 1759223400

michael (eng-sre): One more: add post-deploy audit event that records image digest, signer key id, promotion timestamp, and who triggered. That goes to long-term audit store (90d).

emily (eng-security): Exactly. Also create a short postmortem template if we see any regression: root cause, rollback time, affected services, mitigation.

anna (platform): I'll update the internal runbook and add a quick checklist: KMS key id, promotion commands, canary label, rollback steps, contacts.

jordan (eng-runtime): Build status: ubuntu patch build passed unit tests, running integration now. Will post SBOM and digest when ready.

deploy-bot: ubuntu-22.04-glibc-patch build #123 integration tests passed at 1759223850; SBOM uploaded; image signed with key key-rootfs-v2; digest sha256:abcdef...

emily (eng-security): Great. Proceed with canary per plan. @michael please start the 5% canary at 09:00 UTC.

michael (eng-sre): Roger. Scheduling canary rollout. Will monitor and report in this thread. :thumbsup:

emily (eng-security): Thanks everyone. Keep thread updated with any anomalies.
